A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same flow-matching study. Their text, figures, equations, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across renumbering and reorganization.

before.justification: Sections 3–4 report original velocity-alignment, memorization, hybrid-generation and FID experiments on synthetic and image data.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, supplemented by new FID tables in Appendix C and computational timing measurements in Appendix D.1.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 and Appendix B.1 retain the same EFM procedure: include the generating example in the sampled batch, compute normalized velocity weights, and regress against that target. The inconsistent rewrite of main-text Equation (8) does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The two-moons, Imagenette, CIFAR-10 and CelebA coverage remains. New Appendix C adds benchmark results described in the prose as MNIST, although both tables are captioned FMNIST. Additional image-generation coverage is evident, but the assignment of the two tables to datasets is ambiguous.

E2.justification: The main comparison retains CFM, OTCFM and EFM variants in v1 Figure 5 and v2 Figure 4. The new appendix tables use the existing CFM comparator; no new comparison method is evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported dataset-size sweep drops the 500-sample condition. New Appendix C experiments use FID in a 128-dimensional classifier embedding, additional EFM settings including M=512 and M=1024, and evaluations through epochs 25 and 200. The retained CIFAR-10/CelebA training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 adds a qualitative sensitivity finding for M=2000 and M=5000, reporting nearly identical results to M=1000. Appendix D.1 adds timing experiments varying batch size and EFM sample count. Existing dimensionality and hybrid-trajectory analyses remain.

E5.justification: No new repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimates or significance tests are provided. The added tables contain individual FID values; the new checklist explicitly acknowledges that error bars are not reported.

E6.justification: Appendix C adds two FID tables; for example, Table 2 reports epoch-200 FID of 19.67 for CFM and 16.85 for EFM with M=512. These are new results, not improvements over corresponding v1 experiments. V2 also adds timing measurements and the large-M saturation finding, and removes the 500-sample results from the dataset-size figure.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 revises the product-conditioning derivation with empirical normalization factors and explicit d-dimensional Gaussian/Jacobian calculations. However, its final numerator in Equation (29) drops 1/n. The rewritten main Equation (8) also introduces weights inconsistent with Appendix B.1. The propositions and Appendix B arguments otherwise remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: target stochasticity is not the principal explanation for generalization, failure to fit the optimal velocity matters especially early, and EFM preserves or modestly improves performance. Added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly identifies the unstudied interaction between architectural inductive bias and optimization as a limitation. Section 3.3 also qualifies the late-time interpretation: approximation failure cannot fully explain generalization, whereas v1 says it cannot explain it.

D1.justification: V2 adds a dedicated project-code link, specifies that the same 50,000 generated images serve the train/test FID calculations, and documents NVIDIA L4 timing measurements. Appendix C supplies its U-Net, Adam optimizer and classifier-embedding details. These extend the existing implementation information.

R1.justification: V2 adds research connections including Lukoianov et al. on architectures beyond convolutional models, Sclocchi et al. on temporal regimes, and Boursier, Bonnaire and Favero works on optimization-related limitations. The main positioning relative to stochastic-target and closed-form approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 2 receives localized explanatory and terminology revisions. V2 adds acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist, inserts an additional-experiments appendix, and moves the existing experimental-details appendix from C to D. Most of the scientific narrative and section sequence remain.

P2.justification: V2 adopts NeurIPS formatting throughout, redesigning the title, affiliations, abstract and page composition. V1 Figures 1–2 become a rearranged three-panel Figure 1; the dataset-size plots receive revised legends and explicit sample-count axes. Two FID tables are added, while the existing hyperparameter table and other main figures are retained under new numbers.

improvement.justification: The timing study replaces a vague overhead statement with measured cost scaling, while clearer evaluation details, a project-code link and additional benchmarks modestly strengthen reproducibility and evidence. Ambiguous MNIST/FMNIST captions and introduced equation inconsistencies reduce these gains. The original procedure remains recoverable from Algorithm 2 and Appendix B.1, supporting a limited net improvement.
